headline: Council approved snow-related budget transfers, an Energy Advocate ordinance, and two union contracts.
summary: The council heard the Mayor's State of the City address and a DPW and Police update on snow removal, towing, and ticketing after a major storm. It approved creation of an Energy Advocate position with amendments, two collective bargaining agreement funding transfers, a fire department budget transfer that was later reconsidered and approved with a waived waiting period, a Verizon conduit installation, and withdrew or recommitted several older committee items. It also referred many new items to committees and set committee meeting times for February 9th.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the 01/05/2026, 01/06/2026, and 01/12/2026 meetings by unanimous voice vote.

Approved DOC # 484/25, creating the Energy Advocate ordinance position, with amendments changing the language requirement to English required/bilingual preferred and adding a qualification enforcement clause, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved DOC # 008/26, transferring $100,000.00 from Emergency Management Permanent Salary and Wages to Professional Services, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved DOC # 004/26, transferring $95,279 to fund the SEIU Local 3 Laborers Union CBA, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved DOC # 005/26, transferring $42,552 to fund the SEIU Local 3 Inspectors Union CBA, by unanimous voice vote.
Reconsidered DOC # 008/26 by unanimous voice vote.
Approved DOC # 008/26 again and waived the 30-day holding period by unanimous voice vote.
Withdrew DOC #348/19 (hookah use prohibition) by unanimous voice vote.
Withdrew DOC # 61/20 (Corona Virus-Lawrence Preparedness) by unanimous voice vote.
Discharged DOC #415/16 (license plate reader review) from committee by unanimous voice vote.
Withdrew DOC #415/16 by unanimous voice vote.
Discharged DOC #329/18 (Lawrence Gas Leak Emergency) from committee by unanimous voice vote.
Withdrew DOC #329/18 by unanimous voice vote.
Recommitted seven items (DOC #114/13, #330/14, #217/18, #328/18, #349/19, #356/19, #161/22) back to the Public Safety Committee.
Recommitted DOC # 483/25 (surplus declaration for land at rear of 47 Hamlet Street) back to the Housing Committee.
Approved DOC # 491/25, installation of conduit at Lowell Street near Pole P3043, by unanimous voice vote.

Page # 1 
MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING 
OF THE LAWRENCE CITY COUNCIL 
Tuesday, February 3, 2026 
 
A REGULAR MEETING of the Lawrence City Council was held on Tuesday, February 3, 
2026. The meeting was called to Order at 7:10 p.m. by City Council President, Jeovanny 
Rodriguez. This public meeting of the Lawrence City Council was conducted in person at 
Lawrence City Hall, 200 Common Street and via remote participation. Members of the public 
who attended this meeting were allowed to make comments during the portion of the meeting 
designated for public comment.  
 
He then asked the City Clerk, Eileen Bernal to call the roll:  
Councilor Rosaly Gonzalez [District B] – Present 
Councilor Franklin Miguel [District A] – Present  
Councilor Vivian Marmol [District D] – Present 
Councilor Stephany Infante [District E] – Absent 
Councilor Celina Reyes [Councilor at Large] – Present 
Councilor Gregory Delrosario [District C] – Present 
Councilor Marc Laplante [District F] – Present 
Council Vice President, Ana Levy [Councilor at Large] – Present  
Council President, Jeovanny Rodriguez [Councilor at Large] – Present  
Present - 8. Quorum established.   
 
NOTE: The Roll was called for Councilor Stephany Infante at approximately 7:20 p.m.  
 
The Council President led the assembly in a Moment of Silence and the Pledge of Allegiance.  
Councilor Marmol made a Motion to approve the following three (3) sets of Minutes:  
01/05/2026 Inaugural Meeting 
01/06/2026 Special Meeting  
01/12/2026 Special Meeting  
Her motion was seconded by Councilor Levy. There was no discussion on the Motion and it 
PASSED by a Unanimous V oice V ote.  
 
PUBLIC PARTICIPATION:  
 
The City Council President stated that members of the Public who had signed in for Public 
Participation would be allotted two and a half minutes to speak. He note d that their comments 
should be addressed to the Council as a whole and not to any individual member. Those 
participating were:  
 
H. Maali, 53 Chester Street. Mr. Maali stated that the citizens support the Police Unions. He 
noted that under the impeccable leadership of Chief Aguiler, the Police Department was doing
Page # 2 
well. He also spoke in support of the DPW and the Inspectional Services Department and 
encouraged the city to hire more inspectors. He commended the Public Schools and the 
leadership of Superintendent Ralph Carrero. He praised the Lawrence Teachers and their Union. 
He thanked the Veterans and encouraged the city to hire two new employees in veteran services. 
He encouraged them to activate the council on aging, and to pay the long-term employees as 
much as the new hires. He also spoke in support of Fire Chief Delaney who is doing the best job. 
“Lawrence Always Strong, Always United.”  
 
Richard Russell, 34 Cross Street. Former City Councilor Richard Russell expressed his gratitude 
for Councilor Stephany Infante and her efforts to physically clear snow from several fire 
hydrants throughout her District. He also asked if there were any updates to the tag and tow 
efforts throughout the last snow storm to see if the efforts were effective. He also said that 
because deficit spending is allowed for the Snow and Ice Budget, a lot small vendors are hired to 
plow. Finally, he expressed concern over the current “Blue Light” system which is used to notify 
residents that a snow emergency has been declared and alternate parking is in effect. He stated 
that there are 21 blue lights throughout the city and that is not sufficient.   
 
No other individual sought to address the Council via Public Participation and the Council 
President submitted the names of the Participants to the City Clerk to be preserved as part of the 
record.   
 
Communication from Mayor, City Officials & City Attorney:  
The Council President then noted that per the City Charter, the Mayor would address the Council 
and the City Residents for the Annual State of the City Address. He noted that this is the 
Mayor’s opportunity to speak directly to the community about the progress and challenges the 
City faces.  
 
DOC # 026/26  2026  State of the City Address – Mayor Brian A. DePena  
Mayor Brian A. DePena was present and he addressed the City Council in Spanish. His speech 
was translated into English by his Senior Advisor, Octavien Spanner. The Mayor began by 
stating that the state of the city is strong. He indicated that he hoped to provide the community 
with his vision for Lawrence for the next four years, from 2026 through 2030. He acknowledged 
that the City faces real challenges and economic pressure but indicated that his vision was one of 
sustainable growth and stable finances.  
He noted that the core of his vision is financial stability which would be achieved by responsible 
budgeting and the effective use of state and federal resources. He saw the need to plan not year to 
year, but generation to generation.  
He spoke about equitable, inclusive development that is intentional and not reactionary. He noted 
the need to prioritize housing, economic development and quality of life issues.  
The Mayor also spoke about the schools. He noted that the recent changes to Charter to revise 
the composition of the School Committee put the city in a better position to regain control of the
Page # 3 
schools. He spoke about the collaboration between his administration, the City Council, the state 
delegation, the governor and the Department of Elementary and Secondary Education in that 
process. 
The Mayor also talked about public safety being a priority of the administration. He noted that 
the new Police headquarters would be opening in the immediate future.  
He spoke about the need to maintain services without an increased burden and noted that one 
way he planned to achieve that is by expanding the tax base. The Mayor also spoke about how 
far Lawrence has come and his enthusiasm for where it is going. He noted that when Lawrence is 
united, there is nothing the city cannot achieve.  
RECESS:  
Upon the conclusion of the State of the City Address the Council made a Motion to Recess. The 
Motion was made by Councilor Ana Levy and seconded by Councilor Stephany Infante. The 
Motion PASSED by a Unanimous V oice V ote and the Council went into recess at approximately 
7:40 p.m.  
At approximately 7:55 p.m., the Council made a Motion to Come Out of Recess. The Motion 
was made by Councilor Marmol and seconded by Councilor Levy. The Motion PASSED by a 
Unanimous V oice V ote 
DOC # 025/26 Status and Update regarding Snow and Ice Removal and Emergency 
Notification Policies – Counc. Vice President Ana Levy, Counc. 
Stephany Infante, Counc. Celina Reyes, Counc. Vivian Marmol and 
Counc. Rosaly Gonzalez  
The Department of Public Works (DPW) Director, Jorge Jaime, was present and was invite to 
come forward and speak on this Document. Director Jaime began by noting that the city had 
been hit with a super storm, and that there had not been a storm of this magnitude in over 10 
years, since 2015. He also noted that the city received 20 inches of snow on Sunday, January 25, 
2026 and another 4 inches of snow on Monday, January 26th. He noted that operations to clean 
up this snow is still ongoing over a week later.   
Director Jaime stated that the planning for this storm had started the week prior to the storm. He 
noted that he has been going on Spanish language radio prior to the storm to education residents 
about the odd/even alternate street parking as there was a super storm being predicted.  
Director Jaime also noted that currently, from midnight to 6 A.M. each day they were doing 
targeted clean up to remove snow banks and expand some of the narrower streets to ensure 
traffic can pass and vehicles have parking options. He noted those hours were chosen 
intentionally to avoid interfering with traffic during the day.
Page # 4 
Lawrence Police Captain J. Cerullo was also present and he noted that the Police and the DPW 
had initially met back in October to talk about winter storm strategies during snow events. He 
also noted that the Mayor declared this Snow Emergency on Saturday, January 24th, immediately 
prior to the storm and that vehicles were ticketed on Sunday morning, prior to the snow so that 
they would move to allow for plowing during and after the storm.  
He noted that the towing and ticketing was still ongoing still ongoing today in a targeted manner, 
in the areas that were having the late-night snow removal, and that one of these operations was 
scheduled to occur at midnight.   
Captain Cerullo also noted that there are two tow companies contracted with the city to tow for 
snow related issues. These are Cody’s and Sheehan’s. He also said that a 3rd company, Hook and 
Go is scheduled to come on board in the immediate future. He noted that a lot of tow companies 
will not do snow related tows.  
Director Jaime stated that the city had 107 pieces of equipment out for this storm. He noted that 
the city owns 15 sanders and they were out in operation during this snow event. He also noted 
that some contractors were out for 44 hours straight. He also noted that the failure of residents to 
follow the alternate parking, odd/even requirement made it almost impossible to clear roads or to 
conduct the snow push back. 
Director Jaime also stated that there is a need to be aware of certain safety concerns. The DPW 
needs to ensure that an ambulance or a fire truck can pass. He talked about the current overnight 
operations where the DPW announces during the day that there will be a clearing that night with 
signage and then they focus on the area that night. He also noted that his staff has been working 
incredibly hard and they are tired, but still working all day and will be out again tonight. He also 
noted that he lives here and he is suffering under these same conditions.  
After being granted the floor, Councilor Delrosario stated that when the Blue Lights went on and 
the state of emergency was declared on Saturday, that was the time for enforcement. He wished 
the city had started to tow before the snow. He noted that it has been a week and several parts of 
his district are still not plowed out. He also asked why none of the Councilors were invited to 
participate in any of the snow preparation meetings. He noted that the Council and the DPW are 
a team and that the Councilors face the community every day. He believed their input would 
have been valuable as well as their ability to convey any message back to the public. He also 
expressed his respect for the DPW staff and plow drivers who are still out there plowing even 
today.  
After being granted the floor, Councilor Reyes thanked Director Jaime and his staff. She 
recognized their hard work. She also stated that she received a lot of complaints, specifically that 
residents would see the same trucks pass by two and three times with their plow blades up. The 
other complaint that she received was on the push-backs, and how aggressive some drivers were 
in pushing the snow on to private property.
Page # 5 
Director Jaime addressed the concerns raised by the Councilor. He noted that some trucks are 
just passing through and not all are contractors with the city. He also noted that they have to push 
the snow back as they have to clear the roads. He recognized that this can be frustrating to 
homeowners but it is necessary. He also noted that his DPW Supervisors patrolled certain areas 
to check on the contractors to make sure that their blades were down and that they were working 
on the assigned areas. He also noted that some complaints were not valid, that he had taken 
Councilor Infante out on a drive along and they received certain complaints, but when they drove 
to that street, the area was already done.  
After being granted the floor, Councilor Infante thanked Director Jaime for accommodating her 
on a ride along during the storm. She noted that this is something that she has done several times 
throughout the course of her years as a Councilor. She agreed that some of the complaints were 
not valid and that the DPW had done the best they could under the conditions that they were 
facing, however she also noted that there are things that can and must be improved.  
Councilor Infante noted that residents need to follow the protocol, however, the plow drivers also 
need to follow the protocol too. Specifically, she spoke about how some drivers plowed the 
wrong side of the street, trapping in parked cars and leaving them nowhere to go the following 
day when they would be required to park on the alternate side. She also asked the DPW to not 
take the feedback and criticism from the constituents on this as a personal attack. She noted that 
the Councilors need to serve as advocates for their residents and bringing in that feedback is their 
responsibility, not a personal attack.  
The Councilor did state that she does not like to see when there are differences between the 
treatment of the north side of the city and the south side of the City. She specifically referenced 
the availability of salt/sand on the north side for residents. She stated that after seeing that on 
social media she advocated for her district and it was made available for them too, but she 
thought that should have been automatic and not something she needed to actively advocate for.  
Director Jaime stated that he tries to service the entire city and does not see a north/south 
division.  
After being granted the floor, Councilor Levy stated that she had concerns with some specific 
situations. For example – on East Haverhill Street at Prospect Street, the area to pass is very 
narrow and she was in that vicinity when an ambulance and fire truck were trying to get through 
at the same time and they could not pass each other. She also raised concerns about the quality of 
the snow removal on Fulton Street.  
Director Jaime stated that he is aware of those concerns and they are being address currently.  
Senior Advisor Octavien Spanner also spoke and he addressed the need to educate the public on 
how to better cooperate during a snow emergency and to make sure they know what is required 
of them.
Page # 6 
After being granted the floor, Councilor Levy asked who is responsible to clear out fire hydrants.  
After being granted the floor, Councilor Laplante noted that he represents about 13,000 
constituents and they are not happy with the snow removal effort. He asked about the ticketing 
and tow operation.  
Lawrence Police Captain J. Cerullo stated that 2,553 tickets were issued throughout the course of 
the storm. He also noted that 611 cars were towed to date.  
Councilor Laplante asked for a timeline of how long the snow emergency is anticipated to last. 
Director Jaime noted that the end of the snow emergency was the Mayor’s call and he could not 
speak to that. Director Jaime also noted that the clean-up effort and the targeted ticketing/towing 
to support that clean-up will continue until all streets are addressed.  
Councilor Laplante also asked about the time frame for the clean-up operation, from midnight to 
6 a.m. Director Jaime indicated that this time was chosen so that they operation is not interfering 
with traffic during the day. He was aware that the time-line in the snow emergency ordinance 
was longer than 6 a.m.  
Councilor Laplante also noted that several people compared this storm to the similar storm of 
2015, but he wanted to remind everyone that there are more than 20,000 additional cars in the 
city now then there were in 2015, and that makes the task much more difficult to manage.  
Finally, Councilor Laplante addressed the sidewalks. He noted that homeowners and business 
owners are responsible to maintain the sidewalks. That ISD needs to enforce that and also that 
residents and property owners need to be educated about the responsibility. In closing he noted 
that both the south side and the north side were hit by this same super storm and both areas were 
facing brutal conditions. He spoke of the need to all work together.  
After being granted the floor, Councilor Marmol stated that she wanted to be solution based in 
her approach to this topic. Her goal for the meeting was to recognize the mistakes that were 
made and work to avoid them in the future. She also noted that the Council has not denied any 
budgetary requests from the DPW and if there is something that they need, she wants to hear 
about that. She wants to hear the solutions that they would like to propose to make this better.  
Councilor Marmol specifically asked about the “mass text” program and wanted to know how to 
join that and how to improve that, specifically, how to get more residents to receive that 
notification. She wanted to make sure that the Blue Light notice is on the web page early in the 
process too.  
Director Jaime stated that the DPW needs applicants with commercial driver’s licenses (CDL’s) 
to apply for city jobs. He noted that the city helps pay for these employees to get their CDL, and 
once they have that, they are more marketable and leave the city employment.
Page # 7 
After being granted the floor, Councilor Delrosario stated that the Council has no expectation of 
when this snow emergency will be complete. He stated that there needs to be targeted 
enforcement of the ordinances and rules. He noted that there are school busses and commercial 
vehicles parked on city streets. These should not be parked on the street even when there is not a 
snow emergency. He suggested notifying the bus company or business associated with the 
vehicle for assistance in getting these vehicles off of the streets.  
After being granted the floor, Councilor Infante asked Captain Cerullo about a commercial 
company from North Andover that had actively dumped snow on a property in Lawrence just off 
of South Broadway, at the intersection of State Street and Easton Street. Captain Cerullo 
acknowledged that this had happened earlier in the day. That it was first reported to the fire 
department that several oversized trucks had come to that area and dumped snow. He indicated 
that the dumping took up almost the entire lot and went up over two stories high. He estimated 
that this “Snow Pile” was about 20 feet high. He also noted that ISD, the Police, Fire and the 
Water Department all made a joint response to the location and that a “Cease and Desist” had 
been issued. It was also noted that the snow had originated at the Amazon facility in North 
Andover.  
In summary the Council President noted that 2,553 parking tickets were issued, 611 cars were 
towed, that there was a desire for plow contractors with the city to be better identified with some 
kind of sticker or marking on their vehicles, and that there was a need to make sure that residents 
who want to get on the emergency text chain know how to do that.  
Councilor Infante asked if when the snow emergency is over and the operation is complete, 
could the DPW and Police file a summary with the City Council. She also noted a need to come 
back together to address the shortcomings in the underlying snow emergency ordinance. Others 
agreed that a better, clearer ordinance would be helpful.  
Public Hearings:  
DOC # 484/25 Creation of Ordinance for new position - “Energy Advocate” in the 
Office of Planning and Development – Daniel McCarthy, Planning 
Director [Pending Language from City Attorney]  
The City Council President invited the City Clerk to read the Legal Notice as published into the 
record. Upon the completion of the reading of the legal notice, the Council President opened the 
Public Hearing. Lawrence City Attorney Timothy Houten was present to speak on behalf of the 
item. Attorney Houten noted that this position was a grant funded position and the individual 
hired would perform community outreach with regard to city energy programs.  
As no other individuals wished to speak on this Document as part of the Public Hearing, the 
Public Hearing was closed.
Page # 8 
Councilor Delrosario made a Motion to Approve DOC # 484/25. His Motion was seconded by 
Councilor Reyes.  
After being granted the floor, Councilor Infante stated that she had reservations about the 
position, more specifically who would be hired to fill the position. She approved of the concept 
but she needed the administration to put someone qualified there and she lacked confidence that 
this is what would occur.  
Attorney Houten was present and he addressed the Councilor’s concern. He noted several of the 
qualifications, and he further stated that Anil Navkal would be overseeing the position and would 
be involved in the hiring process. Anil Navkal was also participation in the meeting via zoom 
and he also attempted to address the Councilor’s concern. Mr. Navkal stated that the position is 
too precious to hire someone without qualifications.  
Councilor Infante asked if someone was already in the position. Mr. Navkal said, no, there was 
no one in this position at this time. He noted that Planning and Development staff were assisting 
with the energy related tasks, but no one person focused on this work at this time.  
After being granted the floor, Councilor Laplante asked how the $85,000 salary amount was 
arrived at. He was informed that this was the salary proposed through the grant funding. He also 
asked why the position description in the Ordinance as proposed stated bilingual as a 
requirement. He noted that most ordinance positions state English required and bilingual 
preferred, but not as a requirement. Attorney Houten noted that the bulk of the work to be 
performed by the position was community education and outreach, so the bilingual requirement 
might be justified. Councilor Laplante then stated that he would like to propose a friendly 
amendment to this item – that the language be changed from bilingual required to English 
required, bilingual preferred.  
Councilor Delrosario, as the author of the Motion, noted that he was OK with this friendly 
amendment.  
After being granted the floor, Councilor Infante stated that she would like to propose an 
Amendment to the Motion as well. In section C of the Ordinance as drafted, she would like to 
add, “Any appointment made to the position of Energy Advocate that does not strictly adhere to 
the minimum education and experience requirements set forth in this Section C, shall be deemed 
null and void. Failure to maintain these qualifications or the discovery of the lack thereof shall be 
ground for the immediate removal from the position.”  
Councilor Delrosario, as the author of the Motion, noted that he accepted this second, friendly 
amendment as well.  
As there was no further discussion on the Motion, the Council President called the question. The 
Motion to Approve DOC # 484/25 PASSED by a Unanimous V oice V ote.  
DOC # 484/25 MOTION TO APPROVE     PASSED
Page # 9 
The Council President then announced the pursuant to the newly revised City Council Rule # 4 
that allows for Proclamations and Citations to be Heard when Introduced, Councilor Franklin 
Miguel would be presenting one of his constituents, Mr. Jose Genao, with a city pin to thank 
him for his continued, longstanding efforts to shovel out city fire hydrants and to assist his 
neighbors during snow storms.  
Councilor Miguel then addressed the Council regarding Mr. Genao, and noted that this is 
something Mr. Genao has been doing for over 18 years. He commended Mr. Genao’s empathy, 
collaboration and commitment in repeatedly stepping up to assist his neighbors. Mr. Genao the 
spoke briefly and said he hoped that the recognition motivates others to do the same. He said that 
if everyone works to make the city a better place even with the simple task of clearing off a 
hydrant there will be a positive outcome and a safer city. Muchisimas Gracias   
RECESS:  
At this time, the Council made a Motion to Recess. The Motion was made by Councilor Infante 
and seconded by Councilor Reyes. The Motion PASSED by a Unanimous V oice V ote and the 
Council went into recess at approximately 9:40 p.m.  
At approximately 9:45 p.m., the Council made a Motion to Come Out of Recess. The Motion 
was made by Councilor Infante and seconded by Councilor Reyes. The Motion PASSED by a 
Unanimous V oice V ote 
The Council President then invited Councilor Infante, in her capacity as Chair of the Budget and 
Finance Committee, to give the Committee Report.  
Budget and Finance Committee:  
DOC # 008/26 Transfer Funds [$100,000.00] from Emergency Management 
Permanent Salary and Wages (012910-5110) to Professional 
Services (012910-5300) - Paul Maccarone, Director of Support 
Service, LFD for Chief Patrick Delaney 
Councilor Infante, in her capacity as Chair of the Budget and Finance Committee, noted that 
DOC # 08/26 came up from Committee with a favorable recommendation to approve the item 
and she made that report in the form of a Motion to Approve. Her Motion was seconded by 
Councilor Celina Reyes.  
Ramona Ceballos, the CAFO, was present to report on this Document. She noted that at the 
Committee level, there were questions about the RFP process and she noted that each Councilor 
had a packet on the table outlining that process for them.  
Senior Advisor Octavien Spanner was also present. Councilor Infante asked Mr. Spanner if he 
could expand on the future of the Emergency Management position. He explained that this was 
budgeted as a “position” but at this time the funds were being utilized to pay a consultant to do
Page # 10 
that work. He noted that in the June budgeting season this could be modified back to a position 
or remain as a consultant.  
Also present were representatives from the Golden Thread Agency, LLC the consultant who had 
been doing this emergency management consulting work. The expanded on their credentials with 
regard to both project management as well as public safety related matters.   
There was no further discussion on this Motion and it PASSED by a Unanimous V oice V ote  
DOC # 008/26 MOTION TO APPROVE  PASSED  
 
DOC # 004/26 SEIU Local 3 Laborers Union Collective Bargaining Agreement 
(CBA) – Transfer [$95,279] from General Fund and Enterprise Fund 
Accounts to various salary funds, to fund the CBA – Ramona 
Ceballos, CAFO 
Councilor Infante, in her capacity as Chair of the Budget and Finance Committee, noted that 
DOC # 04/26 came up from Committee with a favorable recommendation to approve the item 
and she made that report in the form of a Motion to Approve. Her Motion was seconded by 
Councilor Celina Reyes.  
Ramona Ceballos, the CAFO, was present and she spoke on this item too.  
The Council President asked the CAFO to please discuss the stipends associated with this CBA, 
specifically those relating to employees having hoisting licenses and CDL’s. He also noted that 
these licenses require a DOT medical certification to ensure that the Driver is medically fit to 
operate the type of machinery. The Council President also stressed that FMCSA Regulations 
need to be complied with.  
After being granted the floor, Councilor Delrosario stated that the city needs to maintain a file on 
all of the CDL’s and make sure that this information is retained together with up-to-date 
information. The CAFO verified that the city does have a list of which employees have these 
licenses. She noted that they are currently verifying that none are expired and are requiring that 
copies of the fronts and back of all of the licenses are on file as well.  
There was discussion on the fact that the city pays for these CDL’s and the drivers often leave the 
city after they get that license. The suggestion was made to require reimbursement for those costs 
if an employee left within a set period of time after getting that license, such as 2 years which 
some private sector employers require.   
There was no further discussion on this Motion and it PASSED by a Unanimous V oice V ote  
DOC # 004/26 MOTION TO APPROVE  PASSED
Page # 11

DOC #415/16 Review of the Police Department’s use of the license plate reader –
